physicalNotes: Radius 0.23802302 Jupiter radii from Livingston et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.484....8L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.484....8L/abstract): 17,016.7 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0239 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Rizzuto et al. 2018 (2018AJ....156..195R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname RIZZUTO_ET_AL__2018): P 19.66365 d
sources.shape: Livingston et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.484....8L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LIVINGSTON_ET_AL__2019): a/R* 51.3; Livingston et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.484....8L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LIVINGSTON_ET_AL__2019): inclination 89.38 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Rizzuto et al. 2018 (2018AJ....156..195R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname RIZZUTO_ET_AL__2018): transit mid-time 2458096.93729 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 65 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
